chapters.title: Chapter 1: The World's Stock Markets at a Glance

lessons.title: Mapping the World's Biggest Exchanges: Size, Listings, and Where India Ranks

children.text: Ask ten people to name the world's biggest stock exchange and most will say the New York Stock Exchange. In March 2026, they would have been wrong. Nasdaq overtook NYSE to become the largest exchange on earth, worth about $35 trillion. Now try a second question. BSE has more than 5,500 listed companies, far more than Nasdaq's roughly 3,450. So is BSE bigger? Not even close. All of India's listed companies together are worth about $5 trillion, roughly one-seventh of Nasdaq alone. Ranking exchanges sounds simple until you ask what exactly you are measuring.

body.text: An exchange is not big because it has many companies. It is big because the companies on it are valuable, heavily traded, or both. Always ask which yardstick a ranking uses before you believe it.

children.text: Three Yardsticks for Measuring an Exchange

markDefs.definition: The total value of shares bought and sold on an exchange over a period, such as a day or a year. It measures how actively a market trades, not how valuable its companies are.
A futures or options contract whose value comes from an underlying asset such as the Nifty 50 index or a stock. Exchanges are often ranked by how many of these contracts change hands.

children.text: Professionals use three different measures, and each tells a different story. Market capitalisation tells you how much the listed companies are worth. The number of listings tells you how many companies have chosen that exchange. Trading activity, measured through
turnover
in shares or the number of
derivatives contracts
traded, tells you how busy the exchange is. An exchange can top one list and be absent from another.

children.text: Yardstick 1: The Biggest Exchanges by Value

The World Federation of Exchanges (WFE) tracks the domestic market capitalisation of member exchanges every month. Its March 2026 data shows a very top-heavy world. The two US giants together are worth more than the next several exchanges combined. After them come Shanghai, Euronext, Japan Exchange Group, Shenzhen and Hong Kong. India is the only country apart from the US and China with two exchanges in the global top 10.

body.text: Exchanges are businesses too. Nasdaq Inc., ICE, HKEX, Euronext and JPX are all listed companies whose shares you can buy. BSE Ltd. is listed as well, but on NSE, not on itself. An exchange cannot neutrally regulate trading in its own shares, so it lists on a rival.

children.text: Exchange Rankings vs Country Rankings

markDefs.definition: When the same company's shares are listed on more than one exchange. Almost every large Indian company, such as Reliance or Infosys, is listed on both NSE and BSE.

children.text: Exchange rankings and country rankings are not the same thing, and mixing them up is a classic beginner error. The US has two giant exchanges, so the country is far bigger than either one. Euronext is one exchange group spread across several countries. And India's two exchanges share most of the same companies through
dual listing

. Reliance Industries is counted once in NSE's market cap and again in BSE's. That is why India can have two exchanges worth roughly $5 trillion each while the whole country is also worth roughly $5 trillion.

body.title: Can you add NSE and BSE?
body.question: NSE's listed companies are worth about $5 trillion and BSE's are worth about $5 trillion. Why is India's total stock market not worth $10 trillion?
options: BSE reports its market cap in rupees, so the two cannot be compared
Most large companies are listed on both exchanges, so adding them counts the same companies twice
SEBI only counts NSE-listed companies in India's official figure
BSE's figure includes foreign companies listed in India
body.explanation: Almost every large Indian company is dual listed on NSE and BSE. Their value appears in both exchanges' market caps. To find a country's total, you count each company once. BSE's figure is often used as a proxy for India's total because it has the widest list of companies.

children.text: The India vs Taiwan Tug of War

In May 2026, Taiwan overtook India to become the world's fifth largest stock market, powered by a surge in chipmaker TSMC on AI demand. India won the spot back by late June as Taiwan and South Korea cooled. Think about how strange that is. India's economy is more than four times the size of Taiwan's. Yet one company's share price swung the ranking between them. Country rankings measure what investors are willing to pay today, not how big or important an economy is.

stats.label: India's market cap
stats.context: May 2026, recovering to $5.05 trillion by late June

body.latex: \text{Market cap to GDP ratio} = \frac{\text{Total stock market capitalisation}}{\text{GDP}} \times 100
body.caption: A quick gauge of how large a stock market is relative to its economy

body.title: Taiwan's market cap to GDP
body.prompt: Using the May 2026 figures, Taiwan's stock market was worth $4.95 trillion and its GDP was $977 billion. What was Taiwan's market cap to GDP ratio, in percent? Round to the nearest whole number.
body.explanation: First put both numbers in the same unit: $977 billion = $0.977 trillion. Then $4.95 trillion ÷ $0.977 trillion × 100 = 506.65%, about 507%. For India, $4.92 trillion ÷ $4.15 trillion × 100 = about 119%. Taiwan's market is worth five times its economy because it hosts globally dominant exporters like TSMC whose profits come from customers all over the world.

body.text: Watch for concentration. TSMC alone makes up about 42% of Taiwan's benchmark TAIEX index. When a single company carries a whole market's ranking, that ranking can reverse just as quickly. A country's position on these league tables is a snapshot of prices, not a report card on its economy.

children.text: Yardstick 2: More Listings Does Not Mean Bigger

India is a world leader by the number of listed companies. BSE alone has more than 5,500. But count is a poor measure of size. A large share of BSE's listings are tiny companies with little trading, and some are suspended altogether. Nasdaq has fewer companies, but several of its biggest names, such as Nvidia, Microsoft and Apple, are each worth more than India's entire top 10 combined. What matters is the average value per company and how concentrated that value is at the top.

cells: Includes many small and inactive companies
Counted as stocks, including multiple share classes of the same company
Includes companies on the NSE Emerge SME platform
Fewer listings, many of them very large

body.title: Average size of a Nasdaq company
body.prompt: Nasdaq's listed companies were worth about $35 trillion in March 2026, spread across about 3,450 listed stocks. What is the average market cap per listed stock, in $ billion? Round to one decimal place.
body.explanation: $35 trillion = $35,000 billion. $35,000 billion ÷ 3,450 = $10.14 billion, about $10.1 billion per stock. Compare that with BSE: about $4.9 trillion across more than 5,500 companies, or under $0.9 billion each. The averages hide huge concentration at the top, but they show why counting listings tells you so little about size.

children.text: Yardstick 3: Where India Leads the World

India may be a mid-sized market by value, but it is a heavyweight by activity. NSE has been ranked the world's largest derivatives exchange by number of contracts traded every year since 2019, according to the Futures Industry Association (FIA). Most of that volume comes from Nifty and Bank Nifty options, which trade in small, cheap contracts that millions of retail traders can afford. India also leads the world in the number of companies going public each year.

body.text: Being the world's busiest derivatives exchange is not a badge of investor success. SEBI's own study found that 93% of individual traders in equity F&O lost money over FY22 to FY24. High contract volume reflects small, cheap, heavily traded options, not the size or quality of Indian companies. This is why SEBI has tightened F&O rules for retail traders since late 2024.

children.text: How the World's Exchanges Came to Be

body.title: Key milestones in the history of stock exchanges

events.title: Amsterdam starts trading shares
events.description: Shares of the Dutch East India Company (VOC) begin trading in Amsterdam, widely seen as the birth of the modern stock market. Amsterdam is now part of Euronext.

events.title: The Buttonwood Agreement in New York
events.description: Twenty-four brokers sign an agreement under a buttonwood tree on Wall Street, the origin of the New York Stock Exchange.

events.title: London Stock Exchange formally established
events.description: Share traders who had gathered in London coffee houses since the late 1600s form a regulated, membership-based exchange.

events.title: BSE is founded in Bombay
events.description: The Native Share and Stock Brokers' Association is formed, later becoming BSE, Asia's oldest stock exchange.

events.title: Tokyo Stock Exchange is founded
events.description: Japan's first stock exchange opens during the Meiji era of rapid modernisation.

events.title: Nasdaq launches
events.description: Nasdaq begins as the world's first electronic stock market, with no trading floor.

events.title: Shanghai Stock Exchange reopens
events.description: China reopens a stock exchange in Shanghai as part of its market reforms. Shenzhen follows soon after.

events.title: NSE starts equity trading
events.description: NSE brings fully screen-based, nationwide trading to India, ending the dominance of BSE's open outcry trading floor.

events.title: Euronext is formed
events.description: The Paris, Amsterdam and Brussels exchanges merge into Europe's first cross-border exchange group.

events.title: GIFT Nifty goes live at full scale
events.description: Nifty futures trading moves from Singapore to NSE International Exchange at GIFT City, Gujarat.

body.title: Asia's oldest exchange
body.textWithBlank: BSE, Asia's oldest stock exchange, traces its origins to the year ___.
body.explanation: BSE began in 1875 as the Native Share and Stock Brokers' Association in Bombay, three years before the Tokyo Stock Exchange was founded in 1878.

children.text: Reading Exchange Data Yourself

BSE shows the total market cap of its listed companies right on its homepage, but in rupees, usually in lakh crore. To compare India with the US or Taiwan, you need dollars. The conversion is simple once you remember that 1 lakh crore is 1 trillion rupees.

body.latex: \text{Market cap in \$ trillion} = \frac{\text{Market cap in ₹ lakh crore}}{\text{USD/INR rate}}
body.caption: Because ₹1 lakh crore = ₹1 trillion, dividing by the exchange rate gives $ trillion directly

body.title: Convert BSE's market cap to dollars
body.prompt: BSE's homepage shows the market cap of all its listed companies as ₹465 lakh crore. USD/INR is 95. What is this in $ trillion? Round to two decimal places.
body.explanation: ₹465 lakh crore = ₹465 trillion. Divide by 95: 465 ÷ 95 = 4.8947, about $4.89 trillion. Notice the currency effect. If the rupee weakened to 100 per dollar with no change in share prices, the same ₹465 lakh crore would be only $4.65 trillion, and India could slip in global rankings without a single stock falling.

body.title: Fix the WhatsApp forward
body.scenario: A message is going around your family WhatsApp group: "India now has the world's biggest stock market! BSE has over 5,500 listed companies, more than Nasdaq or NYSE. NSE is also the world's number one exchange. Add NSE and BSE and India's market is worth $10 trillion, bigger than China."
body.prompt: Identify every error in this message and write a short, polite correction you could post in the group.
body.modelAnswer:
Errors:
1. Number of listings is not size. BSE has the most listed companies, but those companies are worth about $5 trillion together, far less than Nasdaq's roughly $35 trillion.
2. NSE is number one by derivatives contracts traded, not by the value of its listed companies. By market cap, it sits in the lower half of the global top 10.
3. You cannot add NSE and BSE. Most large companies are listed on both, so adding them counts the same companies twice. India's total is about $5 trillion.
4. India is not bigger than China. By country, India ranked fifth or sixth in mid-2026, behind the US, mainland China, Japan and Hong Kong, and swapping places with Taiwan.

Suggested reply: "India's markets are genuinely impressive. BSE has the most listed companies in the world and NSE is the world's busiest derivatives exchange. But by value, India is about $5 trillion, around fifth or sixth globally. NSE and BSE share most of the same companies, so we can't add them together."

body.title: Build your own exchange snapshot
steps: Open the WFE statistics portal and note the latest domestic market cap for Nasdaq, NYSE, Shanghai, JPX and NSE.
Go to the BSE homepage and note the total market cap of BSE-listed companies in ₹ lakh crore.
Check today's USD/INR rate and convert BSE's figure into $ trillion.
Compare India's dollar figure with Taiwan's and Hong Kong's to see where India ranks this month.
Repeat this once a quarter and note whether rank changes came from share prices or from the rupee.

cards.definition: The total value of domestic companies listed on an exchange. The WFE uses this to rank exchanges by size.
The total value of shares traded on an exchange over a period. It measures activity, not company value.
When a company's shares are listed on more than one exchange, such as Reliance on both NSE and BSE.
Total stock market value divided by GDP, times 100. Taiwan was about 507% and India about 119% in May 2026.
World Federation of Exchanges. The global industry body that publishes standardised statistics on member exchanges.
Futures Industry Association. The derivatives trade body whose annual volume rankings have placed NSE first by contracts traded since 2019.

points: Exchanges can be ranked by market cap, number of listings or trading activity, and each gives a very different league table.
By value, Nasdaq (about $35 trillion) overtook NYSE (about $31 trillion) in March 2026. Shanghai, Euronext, JPX, Shenzhen and Hong Kong follow.
Exchange rankings are not country rankings. You cannot add NSE and BSE because most companies are listed on both.
By country, India ranked fifth or sixth in mid-2026, trading places with Taiwan as TSMC's rally swung the ranking.
BSE has the most listed companies in the world, but count says little about size. Nasdaq's average stock is worth about $10.1 billion.
NSE has been the world's largest derivatives exchange by contracts traded since 2019, and India led the world in IPO count in 2025.
To compare India globally, convert BSE's market cap from ₹ lakh crore to $ trillion by dividing by USD/INR. A weaker rupee lowers India's rank even if share prices do not move.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and is not investment advice. Figures are drawn from the World Federation of Exchanges, FIA, EY, SEBI, the IMF and published news reports as of the dates stated, and may be revised. Market cap rankings change daily with share prices and currencies. Companies and exchanges named are illustrative examples, not recommendations.
